_about: The sights. clickMoa is what one click of elevation moves the strike, windageClickMoa one click of windage, in minutes of angle; clicks is the travel each way from the middle. zoom is the magnification range; fovFtAt100 the field of view in feet at 100 yards at the lowest and highest zoom. frontPostMoa is the front post's width over the sight radius (how wide it looks against the target); apertureMoa the rear ring's lit circle and notchMoa the rear notch's width as the eye sees them; dotMoa a red dot's size. leaf is a sliding rear leaf: its marked settings, the service load it was cut for, and each setting's angle above the 100 m setting, derived with the engine (leaf545: the same leaf on the 5.45x39 rifle, cut for its own load). notchDepthMoa is the rear notch's depth as the eye sees it; stemWidthMoa a bead's stem; a drop reticle's chevronHalfWidthMoa and markHalfWidthMoa are its drawn widths. aimWanderFactor scales the drawn wander of the aim through this sight (1 where absent). frontBead marks a front sight that is a round bead on a stem rather than a flat post. range-day-twelve: sightRadiusIn is the distance between the front and rear sight, the radius the front post's width is seen over; frontPostIn and apertures (each peep's diameterIn) are the parts' own sizes; frontEars draws the front sight's guards (their inner gap, each one's width, and how far their tops stand above the post); frontStripeMoa and frontStripeTopMoa a glowing stripe on a front post; adjustWords says in plain words where each adjustment is; kind "seeall" is the SeeAll Open Sight, its reticle a triangle whose tip is the aim point, standing across a line that tops a glowing field; a reticle's focalPlane and trueAtPower say where a second-focal-plane reticle's marks are true (at another power p they stand trueAtPower / p times as far apart in angle). tookThePlaceOf names the sight a new one replaced on its rifles without carrying its records (they click differently or sit at another height): a record from before any sight could be chosen, made with the old sight, is never read as the new one's. rearBody is a rear peep's leaf, where it stands far from the eye (its width and how far its top stands above the peep): only the leaf is dark around the peep; a sight without it has its ring close to the eye, dark to the edges of the view. range-day-twelve-b: a rear sight with two peeps (apertures, each with its diameterIn and the apertureMoa it covers seen from the eye) flips between them on the firing line; both stand in the same plane, so the flip moves no shot. frontHood is a round hood around the front post (its inside diameter and its wall, as the eye sees them), centred on the post's tip. range-day-thirteen: collection marks a scope of the scope collection, which moves among the rifles: a rifle offers it when its own scope mounting (data/rifles.json, scopeMount) takes the scope's mount (mount.fits), and its height over the bore on that rifle is the rifle's rail height plus the mount's centerOverRailIn (lib/guns.js works it out and checks it). windageClicks is a scope's windage travel each way where it differs from clicks. A reticle of kind "chevron" is a chevron whose tip is the aim point (chevronBaseWidthMoa wide at its base, chevronHeightMoa from tip to base); of kind "crosshair" a fine crosshair; marksNotDrawn says which of the maker's marks are left out and why. range-day-eighteen: ownScopeOf names the one rifle whose own scope a sight is (not one of the collection: it is offered by that rifle's sights list and mounted as data/rifles.json, scopeMount.ownScope, says); tubeMm is a scope's tube; a crosshair's centerDotMoa is a dot at its center, drawn in its litColor; on a second-focal-plane reticle every mark, a dot included, stands trueAtPower / p times its true size in angle at power p. A reticle of kind "ladder" is the ACSS 22LR G2 (the .22's scope): a lit center dot, a fine line turning into heavy posts at the sides, a post below carrying stadia lines (each its depth, its width, whether it is a barbell with end ticks, and its wind dots' spread), and a pointed lower post; every figure measured from the maker's reticle drawing (public/line.js, ladderMarks).

reticle.about: The ACSS 22LR G2: a red center dot (lit) in a gap of the fine horizontal line, which turns into heavy posts at the sides; no line above the center; below it a post from the 75-yard hold at its top down past five stadia lines (100, 150 and 200 yards drawn as barbells, with end ticks; 125 and 175 plain), a 5 mph wind dot either side of each stadia, then a heavy post with a pointed tip. The maker calibrates the holds "to best fit 36-40gr projectiles at 1000-1200 FPS" with the center dot zeroed at 50 yards, at 6x only. Every mark is drawn at its angle from the maker's drawing; no distance is written beside any of them on the screen.
